parts.text: In this experiment, you will determine the focal length of a converging lens by different methods. Method 1 Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 3.1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Arrange the illuminated object, lens and mirror as shown in Fig. 3.1. Fig. 3.1

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Set the distance D between the mirror and the illuminated object to 40 cm. Move the lens until a sharp image appears on the front of the card, by the side of the illuminated object. Measure the distance f 1 between the lens and the illuminated object. This is a value for the focal length of the lens. f 1 = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 3(a)(ii)
ms.text: move lens backwards and forwards slowly OR move lens slowly

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Set up the lens, illuminated object and screen as shown in Fig. 3.2. Fig. 3.2 Set the distance between the illuminated object and the lens to u = 20.0 cm. Move the screen until a sharp image of the illuminated object appears on the screen.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Measure h O , the height of the illuminated triangle, as indicated in Fig. 3.2. h O = ............................................................... Measure h I , the height of the image of the triangle on the screen. h I = ............................................................... [2]

ms.label: 3(b)(i)
ms.text:
hO between 1 (cm) and 2 (cm)
hI between 3.2 (cm) and 6.5 (cm)

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate a value W using the equation W = h O h I . W = ............................................................... Calculate a second value f 2 for the focal length of the lens, using the equation f 2 = u ( W + 1) . f 2 = ............................................................... [2]

ms.label: 3(b)(ii)
ms.text:
W with no unit and f2 expressed to 2 or 3 significant figures with unit cm
f2 within 10% of f1

ms.label: 3(b)(iii)
ms.text:
hand gets in way of light
mark on screen and measure later OR
use screen with scale OR
use translucent screen and measure at rear

ms.label: 3(c)
ms.text:
statement matching results
values within limits of experimental accuracy/owtte
and values quoted in justification

ms.label: 3(d)
ms.text:
any one from:
mark position of lens on holder
clamp/place rule on bench
ensure screen, lens and object all perpendicular
view rule perpendicularly
repeat and take average
use darkened room/brighter light
